# Source code generated by Claude Code
> [!NOTE]
> This repository contains source code generated by Claude Code. All source code and related materials in this repository, including this `README.md` file but excluding this note, were generated by Claude Code.
> 
> To run the commands below, clone the [configurations](https://github.com/three-edge-coloring-apex-cubic-graphs/configurations) and [discharging-rules](https://github.com/three-edge-coloring-apex-cubic-graphs/discharging-rules) repositories as follows:
> ```bash
> git clone git@github.com:three-edge-coloring-apex-cubic-graphs/configurations.git
> git clone git@github.com:three-edge-coloring-apex-cubic-graphs/discharging-rules.git
> ```


C++20 implementation of the pseudocode in Appendix B of `apex.pdf`, together with the
algorithms of Appendix A of [IKM+26](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24880) that it cites.
Everything is written from the published pseudocode; the authors' original source code was
not consulted.

## Build and run

```sh
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -S .
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure     # fast checks only (parser + Lemma B.1)

./build/verify_b1 -v                           # Lemma B.1, ~0.1 s
./build/verify_b2 --counts-only                # Lemma B.2 wheel counts, all degrees
./build/verify_b2 --counts-only --degree 11    # ... one degree at a time
./build/verify_b2                              # ... plus the verifyNoBadCartwheels assertion
./build/verify_b3                              # Lemma B.3 island construction, ~2h50m
./build/verify_b3 --limit 30                   # ... first N configurations only
./build/verify_b3_reduce                       # Lemma B.3 island construction + semi-D/C check
./build/verify_b3_reduce --limit 30            # ... first N configurations only
```

All binaries expect the repository root as the working directory and use every core
(`std::thread::hardware_concurrency`). Each exits non-zero on a mismatch.

Lemma B.3's island *construction* (`allHomImages`, Algorithms B.4.1-B.4.16, run over all 915
configurations in filename order via `verify_b3`/`verify_b3_reduce`) matches exactly: 109 501
total islands. Full semi-D/semi-C-reducibility verification of those islands (B.1.1-B.1.5 plus
the unpublished semi-consistent-subset fixpoint, see `HANDOFF.md`) is implemented in
`verify_b3_reduce` and has completed end-to-end: every one of the 109 501 islands is semi-D- or
semi-C-reducible, with zero failures. See `HANDOFF.md` for two bugs found and fixed while getting
there — a correctness bug (singleton positions in a semi-matching are independently flippable,
not inert) and a performance bug (redundant candidate-list rebuilding, fixed with a 37x speedup)
— plus the runtimes of both the original and the sped-up full sweep.

### Measured cost of the Lemma B.2 wheel counts

On 8 cores (Apple M-series), `--counts-only`:

| d | wheels scanned | time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 36 140 | 9 s |
| 8 | 174 950 | 35 s |
| 9 | 853 604 | 104 s |
| 10 | 4 188 590 | ~8 min (projected) |
| 11 | 20 639 900 | ~40 min (projected) |

Throughput is roughly 0.12-0.20 ms per wheel and scales with the wheel count, which is
`sum_j (5-j)^(d-1)` candidates for Algorithm B.3.2 plus `5^(d-1)` for Algorithm B.3.1.

On 256 cores, `enumPossibleBadWheels` for d = 10 and d = 11 took 11 s and 34 s respectively
(the 8-core estimates above did not need to be spent). `verifyNoBadCartwheels`, run
end-to-end for the first time, adds 11.0 / 20.4 / 6.4 / 1.5 / 0.2 s at d = 7..11 — its cost
tracks the *surviving* wheel count (4438/4939/2409/567/38), not the candidates scanned to
find them, so the full B.2 sweep (`./build/verify_b2`, no flags) completes in under two
minutes total rather than the ~50 core-hours the d = 10/11 counts alone would project to on
8 cores.

## Notes on reading the pseudocode

* `pdftotext` renders `∞` as the digit `8`. Every such occurrence was checked against a
  rendered page image. Three that matter:
  * `CARTWHEEL_DEGREES = [(5,5),(6,6),(7,7),(8,8),(9,∞)]` in B.3.1/B.3.2 — the `(8,8)` is a
    real 8 and only the last entry is infinite;
  * every `[5,8]`-looking bound in the `degree_pairs` table of Algorithm B.3.5 is `[5,∞]`;
    only `[7,10]`, `[6,6]`, `[6,7]`, `[5,5]` are genuine finite bounds. Taking them literally
    gives 4721 instead of 4438 wheels at center degree 7.
  * Algorithm A.7.2 line 5, where `δ⁺(v*) > 8` really *is* the literal 8.

  In the *file* formats, `∞` is encoded as `0`.
* Configuration files list only the internal vertices, so the rotation of each ring vertex of
  the free completion is reconstructed from the near-triangulation identity
  `next_x(next_y(x)) = y`, with the single remaining link being the corner at the outer face.
  `tests/test_parse.cpp` validates the result via Euler's formula and a face-size census for
  all 915 configurations.
* The boundary-completion step of the free-homomorphism algorithm depends on the target type
  (pseudo-embedding / pseudo-triangulation / pseudo-triangulation with digons). It is a policy
  argument threaded to its single call site inside `fixSingleDegreeIssue` (A.4.7).
* `blockedByReducibleConfiguration` has a centered and an uncentered variant; the center is a
  nullable parameter. Lemma B.1 uses the centered form (A.8.1 passes `head(ẽ)`); B.4.1 uses the
  uncentered form, per the preamble of Section B.4.
* The outer extension K-hat of a configuration (Section 4's `K̂`, the input to `allHomImages`) is
  *not* the free completion with a corner left open. Ring vertices have no `δ_K` in the file
  format at all; the paper gives them the degree range `[5, ∞)` (Lemma 2.2's global minimum
  degree). The construction that reproduces the published counts: start from the free completion,
  **delete every ring vertex**, then give each internal vertex that lost a ring-edge a fresh
  pendant vertex (range `[5, ∞)`, genuinely open) per lost edge, so its degree is restored to its
  exact, already-known `δ_K`. `src/island/outer_extension.cpp` implements this directly from the
  parsed `Configuration` (ring-vertex rows are never populated, so no reconstruction is needed
  there at all -- only `freeCompletion()`, used solely for Lemma B.1/B.2's K-bar matching, needs
  `reconstructRingRotations`'s closed ring cycle).
* Algorithm B.4.6 `labelDarts`'s second branch, transcribed from `pdftotext` as
  `succ(pred(d_{i+1})) != nil ... Propagate(succ(pred(d_{i+1})), R)`, cannot be read literally:
  `succ` and `pred` are inverses (M3), so `succ(pred(x)) = x` always, making the branch propagate
  from one of the cycle's own darts and (since `Propagate` overwrites `LD(e)` unconditionally on
  entry) silently corrupt that dart's own L/R label. Reading `pred` as a `rev` OCR error --
  `succ(rev(d_{i+1})) != nil and != d_i -> Propagate(succ(rev(d_{i+1})), R)`, symmetric with the
  first branch's `succ(d_i)` vs `rev(d_{i+1})` -- is consistent and gives the correct results.
* Algorithm B.1.1 `GetValidParens`, line 13: `pdftotext` renders the outer-pair union as
  `P <- P u {(M+1) u {{1, 2}}}`; taken literally this double-covers position 2 (already the start
  of `(M+1)`'s shifted range) and never covers position `2q`. Reading it as `{{1, 2q}}` -- the
  outermost pair spanning the whole structure, matching the standard recursive construction of
  noncrossing perfect matchings -- is the only reading that partitions `[2q]` without overlap;
  confirmed against the rendered page image (the `q` subscript on `2q` was lost, the same class of
  error as elsewhere in this document).
* Definition 3.5's semi-consistency check ("there exists a semi-matching M ... such that every
  map obtained from phi by switching colours by Kempe chains M also belongs to C") is, read fully
  literally (existential over *every* noncrossing partial matching, including the trivial
  all-singleton one), vacuous: a semi-matching with `t` matches and `s` singletons yields `2^(t+s)`
  reachable colourings (Definition 3.4 lets `M'` range over singletons too, not just matches, so a
  chosen-but-unpaired position is still independently flippable -- it is not inert padding), and
  the trivial all-singleton matching, while therefore *not* actually a free pass, is never among
  `GetPlanarHalfKempes`'s "nonredundant" output for boundary sizes >= 2 in the first place, since
  it's always extendable by at least one pair. Restricting the existential to
  `GetPlanarHalfKempes`'s maximal family (as B.1.1/B.1.2's placement right before this definition
  implies) is confirmed to be the intended, non-vacuous reading -- verified empirically (searching
  over *all* noncrossing partial matchings removes nothing at all, for any island tested) and by
  the fact that treating singletons as independently flippable, not inert, was itself a real bug
  (see `HANDOFF.md`'s account of the K029 diagnosis) that silently made the semi-consistency check
  too permissive.

## Cross-checks

* `verify_b1 --no-block` disables the "blocked by a configuration in K-bar" filter and yields
  \|R*\| = 1208 with max charge 6, confirming the filter is exercised rather than inert.
* 365 of the 747 combined rules contain a digon, so the digon-specific machinery
  (B.2.2/B.2.5/B.2.11-B.2.13) is on the critical path.
* \|K-bar\| = 2150 = 2 x (915 + 160): 160 of the 915 configurations have one cut vertex and so
  yield two extensions each, and every extension is taken together with its mirror.
